title: Concept Drills — Recent Trends in Physics (Class 11 Physics)
subject: physics

questions.question: How does a solar cell convert light to electricity, and why is a p–n junction essential?
questions.solution: Photons with energy above the gap excite electrons from valence to conduction band, creating electron–hole pairs. The p–n junction's built-in electric field sweeps electrons to the n-side and holes to the p-side, separating the pairs before they recombine — that separation drives current through the external circuit. Light creates carriers; the junction sorts them.

questions.question: Why do gold nanoparticles appear red or purple instead of gold, and what general principle does this illustrate?
questions.solution: At nanometre scale, a material's properties stop depending only on composition: quantum confinement shifts electron energy levels, and surface effects dominate (most atoms sit at the surface). Nanoparticles' plasmon resonance absorbs particular wavelengths — hence the colour shift. At small size, geometry and quantum effects join chemistry in determining behaviour.

questions.question: What defines a superconductor, and why is the Meissner effect more than just 'zero resistance'?
questions.solution: A superconductor has exactly ZERO electrical resistance below a critical temperature. The Meissner effect goes further: it EXPELS magnetic fields from its interior — an active property, not just perfect conduction (a perfect conductor would trap existing fields). This is what enables magnetic levitation and MRI magnets.

questions.concept: Semiconductor devices — the diode's one-way gate
questions.question: Why does a p–n junction diode conduct in one direction only?
questions.solution: Forward bias (p to +) shrinks the depletion region and lowers the barrier — majority carriers flood across, current flows. Reverse bias widens the depletion region and raises the barrier — only a tiny leakage flows until breakdown. The junction's asymmetric barrier is the one-way valve.

questions.question: Why does an LED produce far more light per watt than a filament bulb?
questions.solution: A filament bulb heats a metal to ~2500 °C and emits a broad thermal spectrum — most energy leaves as invisible infrared heat. An LED emits photons directly from electron–hole recombination across a chosen gap: nearly all the electrical energy goes into visible photons of a selected colour. Direct quantum emission vs thermal radiation is the efficiency gap.

questions.question: Gold nanoparticles are red, while bulk gold is yellow. Why does size alone change colour?
questions.solution: At nanometre scale the surface-to-volume ratio is enormous and electron motion is confined (quantum confinement), which shifts the energies at which light is absorbed — the plasmon resonance moves into the visible. Optical, melting and chemical properties become size-dependent. Nanoscience studies exactly this regime where the size of the object is a material property.

questions.concept: Why medical imaging uses many modalities
questions.question: Why do hospitals keep X-ray, CT, MRI, ultrasound AND PET instead of standardising on the best one?
questions.solution: Each modality measures a different physical quantity: X-ray absorption (density defects in bone), CT (3-D density map), MRI (proton-density/relaxation in soft tissue), ultrasound (acoustic impedance at boundaries) and PET (metabolic tracer uptake). No single contrast mechanism reveals all tissues, so their PHYSICS determines which question each can answer. Choosing an imaging method means choosing which physical interaction to map.

questions.concept: Why particle accelerators need such huge size
questions.question: Why must accelerators grow kilometres long to reach higher energies, instead of just using stronger fields?
questions.solution: Energy gain is q∫E dl — it depends on the field times the PATH LENGTH. Real accelerating fields are limited by electrical breakdown and by synchrotron radiation loss that grows rapidly with energy for a curved path. Since E cannot be raised arbitrarily, the path must be lengthened: circular machines grow in radius, linear machines in length. Energy is bought with distance.
